topic: Generic machine-learning method: training related tasks in parallel with shared representations as an inductive bias.
own_question: Can the training signals of related extra tasks improve generalization on a main task? The paper covers backprop, kNN/kernel regression and decision trees.
actual_method_and_evidence: The experiments cover simulated 1D-ALVINN, robot door images, Medis pneumonia risk with future lab tests as extra outputs, and robot sensory prediction. A shuffle test is used to rule out non-informational effects. The paper contains no fusion-plasma or CES content.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Measurements available only offline, such as later values, can serve as auxiliary training targets without being used as run-time inputs.
claim_checks.qualification: The paper demonstrates this on pneumonia and robot domains only. Our study did not implement multitask training. This can serve as a background concept only, not as support for our L5 target design or our results.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: The concept is that future or non-operational features may be used as training outputs but not as inputs. This parallels our rule that neither current F nor future L5 is an online input. The parallel is conceptual only.
validation_if_relevant: The paper uses repeated runs with early stopping on halt sets. This is unrelated to our KSTAR validation designs.
forbidden_inferences: Do not claim multitask learning helps CES nowcasting.
Do not treat L5 as evidence that we used multitask learning.
Do not transfer the reported percentage gains to our setting.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Optional. Cite only if the theory section discusses offline-only quantities as training signals versus run-time inputs. Otherwise omit.
source_scope_note: All extracted page texts supplied; figure/equation visual validation remains separate
